name: Groundnut Stew (Maafe)
summary: Tender beef or chicken simmered in a rich peanut and tomato sauce with sweet potato, served over rice.
story: Groundnut stew is cooked across West Africa under many names, including maafe in Mali and Senegal and domoda in the Gambia. It is an everyday family dish and a favourite for sharing, usually eaten with rice.

items.name: beef stew meat or chicken thighs

steps.title: Brown the meat
steps.text: Season the meat with salt and brown it in hot oil in batches for 6-8 minutes until deeply coloured on all sides. Remove and set aside.

steps.title: Soften the aromatics
steps.text: In the same pot, fry the onions for 6 minutes until soft and golden. Add garlic and ginger and cook one minute until fragrant.

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Stir in tomato paste and chopped tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes until darker and thick, with the oil showing at the edges.

steps.title: Add stock and meat
steps.text: Return the meat, add 2 cups of stock and the scotch bonnet. Cover and simmer gently for 30-40 minutes for beef (20 minutes for chicken), until the meat is nearly tender.

steps.title: Make the peanut slurry
steps.text: Whisk the peanut butter with a cup of warm liquid from the pot until smooth, then stir it back into the stew. This prevents lumps.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the sweet potato and carrots and simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is thick, with a layer of reddish oil on top. Stir often to avoid sticking.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Taste and adjust salt. Remove the pepper and serve over rice.

tips: Use unsweetened natural peanut butter, as sweetened types spoil the savoury balance.
Stir regularly once the peanut butter is in because it catches on the bottom.
Skim off the oil if you prefer a lighter stew, or leave it for flavour.
It tastes even better the next day.

swaps.swap: Freshly ground roasted peanuts are the most authentic; for a nut-free version, sunflower seed butter gives a similar creaminess but a different taste.
Chickpeas and extra sweet potato make a vegan version; cook for about 20 minutes only.
